title: Do you set the trait "Preserve TP" in your game?

posts.author: Sasuke_KANNAZUKI
posts.body:
TP (tactical point) is the feature used in RPG Maker VX Ace, MV and MZ.
By default, the TP is set between 0 and 25 at the start of a battle,
and become 0 after end the battle.
(i.e. TP is always 0 except during the battle.)
On the other hand, when you set the trait "Preserve TP",
TP is not reset at end of the battle and TP is not changed at the beginning of the battle.
I conducted a survey on the Japanese forum to see if you adopt "Preserve TP",
and I found that the majority(70%) of people adopt "Preserve TP".
And I actually guess RPG Maker developers (esp. Yoji Ojima) assume to quite a few people adopt "Preserve TP",
because in the default menu scene of RPG Maker MZ, TP is displayed regardless of whether one adopt "Preserve TP" or not.
How about your game? Do you adopt "Preserve TP"?
And why you adopt(or not adopt) "Preserve TP"?
I don't adopt "Preserve TP".
When I was creating Japanese sample game of RPG Maker VX Ace, I adopted "Preserve TP" at first.
However, developers asked me not to adopt it, because all of sample game creator adopted it.
So I switched not to adopt it.
Based on this experience, I don't adopt "Preserve TP" also in the game I created after that.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
I do not use that option.
I've played games which worked both ways - in my game, TP is not used for ultimate/limit break-style moves, so it's not something that I want my players to build up and save for the perfect occasion.
I mean for it to be used frequently during each battle, like MP, so it resets each time.

posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
I don't adopt Preserve TP for one simple reason:
I have equipment which will preserve TP for you, but it's a trade off.  Such equipment is generally weaker than what is available to the player in exchange for being able to "store" their most powerful skills.
But, by and large, the most powerful skills in my game are meant to be built up over the course of a long battle, because they are "game changing" in terms of power.  They are designed to be used to shift long and drawn out battles into ones that give the player a chance to end things quickly or give them extra leeway in combat.
The player isn't even meant to get any ability to "Preserve TP" until a little later in my game or they've jumped through very specific (and mostly annoying) hoops to get that ability.  The first piece they can conceivably pick up is a sword called "Frustration", which requires the player kill 792 slimes (99 each of the 8 types of slime) to obtain.  This sword also doubles TP gain on top of preserving it.  Though, it has like 40 less Attack than swords for that stage of the game (It's officially a Tier 11 Sword, which makes it good if you get it early, before you see Tier 9 stuff, but if you don't get it until you're seeing Tier 11 stuff, it's pretty weak).

posts.author: Kes
posts.body:
I've done both, with variations.
In one game a couple of characters could have well more than 100TP (by levelling up) but that was for specific tactical reasons.  It seemed to me, though, that other than that specific game, there was no real point in having actors accumulate it.  I want it spent on skills, not being forever increased by spamming Attack.
My last game and my current project do not preserve TP BUT as a player I can't stand starting at zero and not being able to use a skill for at least one, possibly two turns, by which time I hope the battle is over.  So what I've done is ensure that actors always start a battle with 11 - 18 TP.

posts.author: AphoticAmaranth
posts.body:
I've done both. It depends on the game, as well as how TP is used.
In a couple of my games where I use TP as a limit break gauge, I use preserve TP, but reset it to 0 if the player chooses to rest and fully recover the party. It's up to the player to decide if they wanna hoard TP or play it safe and rest.
In Ascentower 2, where I used TP as a resource for regular skills, I don't preserve it. This means that unlike MP, there's no point in hoarding it for future battles, so players don't end up attack spamming regular mobs. There's also items and skills that can affect starting TP.
I've also done a couple of games where I fully heal the party after each battle and repurpose TP for something else, and thus preserving it would be irrelevant.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body: Depends on the game. Sometimes I do, sometimes I don't. My sideproject has it, my main project doesn't. Depends on what I need for my mechanics.

posts.author: lianderson
posts.body: Preserved it, removed the whole damage taken equals more, and then renamed it stamina.

posts.author: Erif
posts.body:
No, I don't use it since I use a very different approach.
My TP charges faster when you're guarding. Or by manually recharging it. And since there are ways to regain a set amount of TP, i think that function is somewhat uselss in my case.

posts.author: KirbyFan637
posts.body: Depends on the type of game I am making. In my current project, I have Preserve TP on as it is used for Specials, which are some of the strongest attacks in the game but cost a lot of TP, so the player can build the TP over battles. In other projects where I did not do something like this, I just did not need to use Preserve TP, so it used in those projects.

posts.author: Robro33
posts.body:
For me, TP is used for Weaponskills like how it is FFXI and how it used to be in FFXIV.
I preserved TP on all actors at first, but i later settled on that being a passive for a specific class since that class' entire identity is that its the "Master of Weapons" and can go a step beyond what others are able to do with their TP and weaponskills

posts.author: Slaughty
posts.body:
It really depends on what you are trying to achieve.
I don't in my current project. TP is used for double/triple/quadruple techs and are some of the most powerful skills. To keep the player from just spamming them, TP is reset every battle. This way the player can't just steam roll every enemy but feels really powerful and clever when they use a double tech.

posts.author: RCXGaming
posts.body:
I use Preserve TP because I want my players to stock TP to use powerful moves even when they can't use MP moves. It goes up to a maximum of 400 per character and goes up by 5 exactly for every action, so having that go to 0 after every fight would be quite frustrating.
I'm not worried about the power of the skills themselves that use TP because there are other checks and balances to make them viable without being overpowered.

posts.author: TG22
posts.body:
Each character in my game has a different TP system. Some will preserve it some won't.
For example I have a non-magic healer that always start the battles with 100 (the maximum amount), she cannot do anything to recover any of them, and so you must be careful to not run out of TP, or you cannot heal anymore.

posts.author: Sasuke_KANNAZUKI
posts.body:
Thank you for so much helpful comments.
I understand you guys consider the advantage of "Preserve TP" well
to  determine whether to adopt or not.
(I'm still welcome to post new comment to tell your opinion.)

posts.author: Maliki79
posts.body:
TP in my game is used for PC specific moves and while are fairly useful, not meant to be OP.  That said, I have TP start at 0 every battle, but can be raised to 25 (the smallest useable amount) after about 2-3 battle rounds.
So building TP is a part of my battle's strategy.
I did consider having PC start with TP equalling their levels ala Wild Arms, but decided against it.

posts.author: Rosemar
posts.body: In my current project I don't use preserve TP, in fact I have an event running at the start of every battle to set all TP to 0 because I use TP as a "limit break" meter. Something you build up to for huge effects when the battle is tough, and I didn't want players farming TP in normal battles and then unleashing it all on an unsuspecting boss.

posts.author: Seacliff
posts.body:
I typically preserve TP in games where I heavily modify how TP works, typically through the game's code.
I almost always rework TP in one way or another though. I'm not much of a fan on how it plays by default.

posts.author: MoonWolfV
posts.body: I use it for limit break type skills. I prefer to retain the TP so the player doesn't have to attempt to build it up all over again in each battle.

posts.author: kirbwarrior
posts.body:
I've used it plenty of times in my games. I've
never
used the regular option but instead use a plugin to have better control over starting TP because it being completely random doesn't ever work with what I'm going for
especially
at 0-25 (it would be one thing to have something like 20-25 or 0-5 but that's such a huge spread).
